title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — each dies/rises his own; deny-in-person = deny Adam's/Christ's death/rising imputed
pass_a_gloss: He clarifies the denial: each dies and rises his own formal death/rising. Denying we die in Adam's person means denying we die by Adam's death imputed; denying we rise in Christ's person means denying we rise by Christ's resurrection imputed—read from the prior words.
pass_b_english: I speak, then, of the death by which each dies, and of the resurrection by which each formally rises. And when I deny that we die in Adam's own person, I mean nothing else than that we die by Adam's own death imputed to us; when I deny that we rise in Christ's own person, nothing else than that we rise by Christ's resurrection imputed to us—as is plain from the very words that went before.
source_text: Loquor igitur de morte qua quisque moritur, de resurrectione qua quisque formaliter resurgit. Nec aliud volo, cum nego nos mori in ipsa Adami persona, quam nos mori ipsa morte Adami nobis imputata; cum nego nos resurgere in ipsa Christi persona, quam resurgere resurrectione Christi nobis imputata, ut patet ex verbis ipsis antecedentibus.

lemmas.gloss: by Adam's death imputed to us
